result.summary: The layout is mostly coherent, but the promotional banner has severely low-contrast white text on a pale green background, and several horizontally scrolled/cut-off elements plus inconsistent favorite-icon styling make the page look unfinished.

issues.description: The promo banner's white text ('3 free deliveries for you' and 'Use code TALLINN3 at checkout · min. order €10') sits on a very light mint green background, making it nearly illegible and far below WCAG contrast minimums.
issues.suggestion: Use dark green/near-black text on the light mint background (or keep white text on a saturated green fill) to reach at least 4.5:1 contrast.

issues.description: The third card in 'Fastest near you' ('Trattoria Piccol...') is clipped hard at the screen edge with its title truncated mid-word and no ellipsis or partial-peek framing, so it reads as broken rather than scrollable.
issues.suggestion: Add consistent horizontal padding/peek for the carousel, truncate labels with an ellipsis, and ensure card widths align to a grid so the cut-off item clearly signals scrollability.

issues.description: The favorite (heart) buttons are styled inconsistently: the Tokumaru Ramen card uses a white circular background with a dark outline heart, while the pizza card below uses a dark circular background with a white heart.
issues.suggestion: Standardize the favorite button treatment (same background, icon color, and size) across all restaurant cards.

issues.description: The category filter chip row is cut off at the right edge with a sliver of the next chip visible, giving an accidental-clipping appearance.
issues.suggestion: Add a fade/gradient mask or trailing padding so partially visible chips read as an intentional scroll affordance.

issues.description: The second 'Popular right now' card is abruptly clipped by the bottom tab bar with no fade or spacing, and its title/metadata are not visible at all.
issues.suggestion: Add bottom content inset equal to the tab bar height so cards scroll cleanly beneath it rather than appearing truncated.

issues.description: The notification bell's red dot indicator conveys unread state by color alone and has no visible text label or count.
issues.suggestion: Add an accessible label (e.g. 'Notifications, 1 unread') and consider a numeric badge.
